places.name: Huelva
past: Founded in Roman times about a forum. Parts of the ancient street grid survive in the core; medieval lanes and subdivided plots grew around them.
The town outgrew its walls. The new circuit keeps 74% of the old wall and runs out only where the suburbs had spread.
5 houses were pulled down to make way for the wall.
A great fire burned 11 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.
A great fire burned 8 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.
The town outgrew its walls. The new circuit keeps 92% of the old wall and runs out only where the suburbs had spread.
The walls were rebuilt on the new trace: earthen ramparts faced in stone, angled bastions and a ditch; 48 houses outside were cleared for the glacis.
A citadel was raised astride the walls on the northern side; 23 houses of the old quarter were razed for it and its glacis, and a garrison quartered there for good.
A great fire burned 8 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.
The old tower keep was rebuilt as a great castle on the same ground.
The parish church was pulled down and rebuilt on its own ground as a great minster.

places.name: Vado de Mora
past: The bishop's cathedral and its burg stood on the dry rise; below, the count founded a merchants' town on the waterfront. For a generation they had two councils, then one.
A new parish church was built for the growing quarter.
Walled.
A great fire burned 25 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.
Besieged; the suburbs outside the gates were burned to deny the enemy cover, and grew back after the peace.

places.name: Puente Real
past: Founded in Roman times about a forum, on the rise above the river. Parts of the ancient street grid survive in the core; medieval lanes and subdivided plots grew around them.
The ford was bridged in stone.

The town outgrew its walls. The new circuit keeps 78% of the old wall and runs out only where the suburbs had spread; 2 stretches of the old wall inside were pulled down for a street along their line.
A great fire burned 24 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.
A great fire burned 18 houses; it was rebuilt in stone.

places.name: Nuestra Señora de la Cinta
past: Farms and an alehouse about a green where the roads meet; a weekly market was granted in its second age.
5 houses were pulled down to make way for the wall.
Walled.
Besieged; the suburbs outside the gates were burned to deny the enemy cover, and grew back after the peace.
The walls were rebuilt on the new trace: earthen ramparts faced in stone, angled bastions and a ditch; 12 houses outside were cleared for the glacis.
A citadel was raised astride the walls on the eastern side; 27 houses of the old quarter were razed for it and its glacis, and a garrison quartered there for good.
